statement: The supplied sources contain no derivation of the Kullback–Leibler divergence. In mathematical statistics, the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence (also called relative entropy and I-divergence), denoted D_KL(P || Q), is an asymmetric statistical divergence on the space of probability distributions measuring the difference between distributions P and Q (the general defining sum/integral is omitted in the source text's truncation, though closed forms are given for specific families, such as exponential families where D_KL(theta_1 || theta_2) = (theta_1 - theta_2)^T mu_1 - A(theta_1) + A(theta_2)).

symbols.meaning: Kullback–Leibler divergence (relative entropy) of distribution P with respect to Q
canonical natural parameters of an exponential family distribution
mean parameter vector E_{theta_1}[T(X)] = nabla A(theta_1)
Fisher information metric (Hessian of relative entropy at theta = theta_0)

properties.property: Relative entropy is an asymmetric statistical divergence rather than a metric, such that in general D_KL(P || Q) != D_KL(Q || P).
properties.why: It generalizes squared distance rather than linear distance and does not satisfy the triangle inequality or symmetry.

properties.property: Relative entropy achieves an absolute minimum of 0 when P = Q.
properties.why: The divergence vanishes for identical distributions, causing its first derivatives with respect to distribution parameters to vanish at theta = theta_0.

properties.property: Up to second order under small parameter deviations Delta theta, D_KL(P(theta) || P(theta_0)) = (1/2) Delta theta_j Delta theta_k g_jk(theta_0) + ..., where g_jk is the Fisher information metric.
properties.why: The vanishing first derivatives at theta = theta_0 leave the positive semi-definite Hessian matrix to define a Riemannian metric on parameter space.

properties.property: Convergence in KL divergence (P_n ->^D P) implies convergence in total variation (P_n ->^TV P).
properties.why: Pinsker's inequality entails that vanishing relative entropy bounds and forces total variation distance to zero.

properties.property: Mutual information between random variables X and Y equals the relative entropy of the joint distribution from the product of marginals: I(X;Y) = D_KL(P_{X,Y} || P_X * P_Y).
properties.why: It quantifies the divergence between the joint distribution P_{X,Y}(x,y) and the independent distribution (P_X * P_Y)(x,y) = P_X(x)P_Y(y).

properties.property: For distributions in the exponential family, D_KL(theta_1 || theta_2) = (theta_1 - theta_2)^T mu_1 - A(theta_1) + A(theta_2).
properties.why: The divergence evaluates directly from canonical parameters theta_1, theta_2, log-partition function values, and mean parameter mu_1 = nabla A(theta_1).

properties.property: Self-information of an event m for a discrete random variable can be represented as I(m) = D_KL(delta_im || {p_i}).
properties.why: It measures the relative entropy of the distribution from a Kronecker delta representing certainty that i = m.

assumptions.assumption: The support of distribution P is contained within the support of distribution Q (e.g., [A, B] enclosed within [C, D] with C <= A < B <= D for uniform distributions).
assumptions.breaks_when: The support of P extends into regions where Q has zero support or probability density.

assumptions.assumption: Regularity conditions on the parameter derivatives of p(x, rho) hold (existence of the first three derivatives of log p and integrability of dominated derivative bounds).
assumptions.breaks_when: The density p fails to be thrice differentiable with respect to the parameter or the derivative integrability bounds fail to be finite.

assumptions.assumption: Both distributions belong to the same exponential family with shared reference measure h(x) and sufficient statistics T(x).
assumptions.breaks_when: The compared distributions have different base measures or incompatible sufficient statistics.

failure_modes.signature: KL divergence is undefined or infinite
failure_modes.cause: Distribution Q assigns zero density or probability to outcomes that have non-zero probability under distribution P.
Treating relative entropy as a symmetric distance metric or assuming satisfaction of the triangle inequality.

failure_modes.signature: Metric tensor g_jk(theta) is non-invertible / singular
failure_modes.cause: The distribution parameterization theta contains non-identifiable or redundant directions, leaving the Hessian positive semi-definite but not strictly positive definite.
